reviewer: Fable 349a plan review (D4 approved); owner policy
review: security Go bug fixed in Rust
reason: Go's postAuth treats forgot-password/begin's 200 decoy as a successful authentication and clears ip:/user:/ip_user: lockout keys, so four wrong passwords plus one begin call reset the counter indefinitely. Rust writes Go's success attempt row but never clears lockout keys for this response.

reviewer: Fable 349a plan review F1; owner policy
review: security Go bug fixed in Rust
reason: Go derives the lockout/spray username with a whole-body json.Unmarshal while handlers accept trailing data, so `{...} x` authenticated with an empty username: no lockout check, no escalation, spray blind. Rust uses each route handler's own first-value decode (login ingress::Login; forgot-password ingress::fields email). Guest-invite is the exception: its threat username is always "" (attempt row, captcha binding and rate/ip rules), because the accept body carries no identity and the handler rejects an email field; Go's extractMeta (and a handler decode) let a caller record a failure against any victim (Fable #381 review). Test: guest_invite_oracle::guest_post_threat_username_keys.

reviewer: Fable 349a plan review F1; owner policy
review: security Go bug fixed in Rust (HTTP only)
reason: Go skips the lockout step when the username is empty. HTTP admission checks the ip: key alone in that case, so a spray-armed ip: lock always applies.

reviewer: Fable 349a plan review F2; owner policy
review: security Go bug fixed in Rust
reason: Go keys /auth/refresh on the body email field or the unverified JWT email, so {"email":victim,"refresh_token":<own valid token>} clears the victim's lockout and forged JWTs escalate any account. Rust keys only the email claim of a refresh token that verifies; otherwise only the ip: key is checked.

review: security Go bug fixed in Rust
reason: Go's captcha token is unbound and reusable for 120 s. Rust's MAC binds answer|exp|source IP|route|username (digits-only answer and exp). A verified token is claimed once per auth process before the pipeline runs and released when the pipeline refuses the request, in a bounded in-memory used set (65 536 entries; full refuses). A restart empties the set, so a token accepted before a restart is accepted once more within its remaining 120 s (still bound to IP, route and username); with several auth processes a token is accepted once per process (production runs one).

review: security Go bug fixed in Rust
reason: Go answers a failed token before the pipeline, so failed checks are never rate limited or tarpitted. Rust runs the pipeline first (tarpit, rate limit, lockout, spray; no captcha threshold); its refusal wins, otherwise 403 CAPTCHA verification failed. A failed single-use claim counts as a failed token. A failed token the tarpit refuses still writes Go's `captcha_needed` attempt row (not `tarpit_applied`, which the outcome CHECK rejects), so the tarpit count matches Go. A verified, claimed token runs Go's skip step.

review: security Go bug fixed in Rust
reason: A rate-limited (429) guest-invite accept writes no auth_attempts row, so a flood of limited requests cannot fill the table.

Go stores the whole username in auth_attempts; a name past the username index limit fails the insert, so the failure row is silently lost and spray/CAPTCHA/tarpit undercount. #433 truncated HTTP names to 255 bytes, which collapsed distinct long names for detect_spray. Rust now stores, for every protocol, names up to 255 bytes unchanged and a longer name as its first ≤222 bytes, '#', and 32 hex digits of SHA-256 of the whole name, so distinct names stay distinct. users_email_check admits no '#', so a bounded form is never a stored account name; an account longer than 255 bytes (not excluded by the schema) loses the user-risk join and auth_attempts_self visibility for its rows. A ≤255-byte literal equal to a bounded form shares its spray identity. Authentication and captcha binding see the whole name.
Go derives the captcha key from JWT_SECRET even when empty (a public key). Rust derives only from a non-empty secret; otherwise the key is empty and every solve fails.
An AuthServer without a Gate answers 503 'threat admission unavailable' on every credential route instead of serving it unadmitted.

HTTP maps ip_rules_unavailable, lockout_unavailable, spray_unavailable, rate_limit_unavailable and captcha_unavailable to 403 'Access denied by security policy' with no attempt row and no handler; Go proceeds.

Go stores the whole User-Agent (up to the 1 MiB header limit) in auth_attempts.device_fingerprint and device_registry.user_agent. Rust stores at most 512 bytes (char boundary) in both; device_hash still hashes the whole agent|masked-IP, so device identity and new-device detection match Go. Conditional-access evaluation sees the whole agent.

review: security Go bug fixed in Rust
reason: Go writes one auth_attempts row per refused request (Middleware recordAttempt), so an unauthenticated client fills the table at request rate; a failed CAPTCHA token or a captcha_needed refusal is not even rate limited. Rust writes a refusal row only while the source has fewer rows of that outcome in the window: rate_limited, lockout, spray_detected, geo_blocked and threat_blocked at most one per source per 60 s; captcha_needed, which the tarpit count reads, until max(TARPIT_THRESHOLD, 29)+1 rows in the tarpit window (shared by login, refresh, forgot-password and guest-invite). While traffic continues it also writes one row per window/(2*budget) seconds whenever the source has no captcha_needed row in that gap. Clustered expiry of one burst cannot empty the window only after continuous traffic of at least threshold × gap (gap = window/(2S)); before that the window can briefly hold fewer than threshold rows; that dip closes at request rate, because below S rows every refused request writes a row. The tarpit delay returns to its 15 s cap only after continuous traffic. Outcomes outside auth_attempts_outcome_check run no statement (Go's insert fails). The budget is per source and outcome, not per username: one refusal hides later targeted usernames from that source for 60 s, and clients behind one NAT share a budget; no counter reads these rows, and lockout_escalate and spray_detected audit_log events are unchanged. A rotating attacker (e.g. IPv6 /64) still writes one row per address per minute per outcome and up to the captcha budget per address: bounded per source, not globally. Responses, failure/success rows, lockout escalation, spray, CAPTCHA threshold and the IP rate counter are unchanged. Concurrent refusals racing the first row can each write one: at most the request-pool size per auth instance each time the count drops below the budget (per source and instance, at most S + P rows from the budget branch plus at most P rows per replenishment gap of window/(2S) seconds, i.e. <= S + P*(2S+1) captcha_needed rows per tarpit window under fully concurrent bursts (P = request-pool size); sequential traffic stays <= 3S+1 rows per window; and <= pool telemetry rows per 60 s). Budget-suppressed rows (INSERT writes 0 rows) are counted per outcome and summarized in one stderr line per 60 s per process with the non-zero counts only, in fixed outcome order (no source IP, username or user agent); the first suppression after start is reported at once; counts left after a flood ends are reported with the next suppression at least 60 s after the previous report. The probe needs SELECT on auth_attempts (auth_attempts_admin_read); if RLS narrows it, the budget turns off (Go behaviour).
